newsitem.title: USA: New York NAPM Sept business index fell to 62.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: New York NAPM Sept business index fell to 62.8 pct.

text.p: The National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index of New York-area business conditions fell to 62.8 percent in September from 64.5 percent in August.
"Purchasers in the New York metropolitan area reported that overall business conditions grew at a relatively steady but strong pace in September," said a report issued with the index.
An index reading higher than 50 percent denotes growth, while a reading lower than 50 percent implies a contraction, the report said.
Specifically, business conditions in the non-manufacturing sector fell to 60.8 percent in September from 64.8 percent the month before.
Manufacturing-sector conditions rose to 81.1 percent from 62.2 percent. "Adding to manufacturing strength were fewer purchasers indicating that inventories were too high," the report said.
The prices paid index read 51 percent in September, compared with 49 percent the month before.
Ninety-two percent of NAPM-New York survey respondents rated their suppliers "good" or "excellent."
"Looking forward to the upcoming six months, purchasers' optimism remained high," NAPM-New York said.
